title: Lead validation step: its card on the canvas (#2590)
intro: The card the lead validation step shows on the canvas, the step that replaces each partner workflow's validate_bidding_and_state script (#934). For whoever reads or builds a partner workflow. Settled by Dan on 2026-10-21 in rounds 5 and 6 of six, drawn on the real canvas in place of a Filter card, at its width, beside Code, Branch and Data Store cards. The step's settings panel is settled in lead-validation-node.html beside this file.

requirements.text: The lead validation step is on the canvas: a palette entry, a card, and a settings panel holding the lead id field and an ordered list of checks, each edited with the rule builder, a reason from LEAD_REJECTION_REASONS and what happens when the lead has no value.

chrome.from: https://bidspoke.trypennie.dev/workflows/0630d714-5917-4221-9bcc-ca1fb2d9eba2 (Main Flow (v2), switched off) in view mode, zoomed to 125% on its Filter card, Dan's signed in Chrome, 2026-10-21

frames.title: The card of a step running seven checks, on the canvas at 125%

decisions.decision: Under its title and step ID, the card says how many checks the step runs, "7 checks", and nothing more about them; the details live in the panel.
decisions.why: Round 5: Dan chose "How many checks" over the first check names, and over the reasons it can give.
decisions.check: The card headed "Lead validation" reads, below its header, these three lines first and in order: "Validate bidding and state", "validate_bidding_and_state" and "7 checks".

decisions.decision: The card's header is slate: Tailwind slate 50 (#f8fafc) behind, slate 100 (#f1f5f9) for the rule under it, slate 700 (#334155) for the label, the same three steps every other card's header uses.
decisions.why: Round 6: Dan chose Slate over Fuchsia, Yellow and Sky, a quiet grey blue that reads as a gate rather than an action and is distinct from Parallel's beige (9.9 to 1 contrast).
decisions.check: The header holding "Lead validation" has background #f8fafc and a bottom border of #f1f5f9, and the "Lead validation" label is #334155.

decisions.decision: The card has one way out, labelled pass, as a Filter card's pass: a rejected lead is answered by the step itself and goes nowhere else on the canvas.
decisions.check: After those three lines, the card's only text is "↓ pass": it names no other way out.

idioms: The card is drawn in place of the Filter card in a captured copy of the canvas at 1120 wide, moved to the middle of the narrower pane; the canvas and every other card around it are the product as it is today, not decisions.
The card's icon is a checked box drawn inline; the build uses the matching lucide icon.
